speaker: Doctor
text: Given the large ovarian mass, significant ascites, and shortness of breath, but a normal CA-125, I suspect a benign etiology like a Meigs syndrome. Do you have any history of heart failure or liver disease, and does the abdominal distension fluctuate with your menstrual cycle?

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: No significant medical history. Social history: Non-smoker, does not consume alcohol regularly. Works as a high school teacher.

speaker: Doctor
text: Do you experience any pain when breathing deeply or moving, and have you noticed any swelling in your legs? I also need to check your heart and lung sounds to rule out other causes of your shortness of breath.

speaker: Doctor
text: The combination of an ovarian mass, ascites, and pleural effusion with a normal CA-125 and no other signs of malignancy strongly points to Meigs syndrome. I will now confirm the diagnosis based on these classic triad findings. DIAGNOSIS READY: Meigs syndrome
